newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania seeks quick solution to Ukraine treaty.
newsitem.headline: Romania seeks quick solution to Ukraine treaty.

text.p: Romania's Foreign Minister said on Sunday difficulties remained to be solved in a treaty with neighbouring Ukraine but Bucharest had to overcome them to keep alive its hopes for quick admission to NATO.
"The European and Euro-Atlantic train has a fixed schedule for everyone," Adrian Severin told the state Rompres news agency in the central city of Sibiu.
"If we have no tickets and are not at the station in time we will miss the train, which means virtually the future of Romania. Things are complicated, but the development overall is positive."
The latest round of talks last week in Kiev failed to produce final agreement on the treaty between the two former communist countries. But both sides acknowledged progress.

"The talks were hard but fruitful and constructive. We made significant progress," Ukraine's top negotiator Anton Buteiko told reporters last week in the capital of the former Soviet republic. "But some elements haven't been agreed yet."
The main remaining stumbling block focuses on delineating frontiers in the Black Sea, where both sides are proceeding with drilling for oil and gas.

Romania had earlier insisted on some form of public atonement by Ukraine for the World War Two seizure by the Kremlin of Romanian lands under the 1939 Nazi-Soviet pact. Severin said Romanians had all but put this issue behind them.

"The treaty is difficult. It should balance our concern for the rights of yesterday's Romania with our concern for the interests of today and especially tomorrow's Romania," Severin said. "We should find the right balance. I hope we find it in good time because time is running short."

Romania, along with Slovenia, is lobbying for inclusion in NATO's first eastward expansion, to be announced at a July summit in Madrid. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are viewed as near-certain entrants.
